user_text: Summarize the benefits of code review for a small team.
assistant_text:
# Benefits of Code Review for a Small Team

## Quality & Reliability
- **Catches bugs early** before they reach production, reducing costly fixes later
- **Enforces consistency** in coding style and standards across the codebase

## Knowledge Sharing
- **Spreads expertise** so no single person is the only one who understands a feature
- **Onboards new members faster** by exposing them to existing patterns and practices
- **Reduces bus factor** — the risk of losing critical knowledge if someone leaves

## Collaboration & Communication
- **Encourages discussion** about design decisions and trade-offs
- **Builds a shared sense of ownership** over the codebase

## Learning & Growth
- **Junior developers improve faster** by receiving structured feedback
- **Senior developers stay sharp** by explaining and justifying their decisions

## Practical Advantages for Small Teams
| Benefit | Why It Matters |
|---|---|
| Lightweight process | Even a quick review adds significant value |
| Flexible tooling | GitHub PRs, GitLab MRs, or simple pair reviews work well |
| Low overhead | A 2-person review loop is fast and effective |

## Key Takeaway
For small teams, code review is one of the **highest-ROI practices** available — it improves code quality, distributes knowledge, and strengthens team cohesion with minimal process overhead.
Code review helps small teams catch bugs early, share knowledge, and maintain consistent, high-quality code.

1. **Bug detection** — Reviewers catch errors and oversights before code reaches production.
2. **Knowledge sharing** — Team members learn from each other's feedback, reducing reliance on any single person.
Code review builds a **shared sense of ownership**, encouraging team members to collectively take pride and responsibility in the codebase rather than treating code as individual territory.

user_text: State one risk if reviews are skipped.
assistant_text: If reviews are skipped, **knowledge silos** can form — where only one person understands critical parts of the codebase, creating a serious vulnerability if that person leaves or is unavailable.

Track **defect escape rate** — the percentage of bugs found in production versus those caught during review — to measure how effectively your review process is preventing issues from reaching end users.
Even a lightweight review process can significantly raise code quality and team resilience over time.

• Code review catches bugs early and shares knowledge across the team.
• It builds ownership, reduces silos, and improves overall code quality.
• Even a simple, lightweight process delivers significant long-term benefits.
Code review is a small investment that pays dividends in quality, collaboration, and team resilience.
Code review is only effective if feedback is constructive and timely — overly critical or delayed reviews can slow progress and harm team morale.
Bad or slow reviews can hurt productivity and team morale.
Code review boosts quality and collaboration, but only works well when feedback is timely and constructive.
